## Overview

This [[adyen]] documentation page is a 2026-09-15 snapshot of the Customer Area workflow and server requirements for configuring, accepting, testing, updating, disabling, and deleting Adyen webhook subscriptions. It covers company, merchant, and merchant-group scope, while recommending company-level subscriptions with merchant inclusion or exclusion to reduce duplicate configurations.

## Key takeaways

- Processing requires a merchant server endpoint, Customer Area subscription setup, and successful acknowledgement of received events. The endpoint and environment requirements, supported methods, ports, authentication inputs, event selection, and optional additional settings are routed to the detailed sections below.
- Adyen requires HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or 1.3 for webhook endpoints; the captured page lists environment-specific ports and says the endpoint URL configured in Customer Area must be public. OAuth 2.0 is documented only for Standard webhooks, and its access-token TTL must be at least 3599 seconds.
- Every webhook event must receive a successful HTTP response, such as `200` or `202`, within 10 seconds. Otherwise, the page says all webhook events to that endpoint enter the retry queue; acknowledgement is separate from the further handling steps linked by the page.
- Customer Area configuration testing and a recommended test-payment correlation exercise precede live setup. Test configuration does not prove production delivery, business outcome, or current account eligibility.
- Test webhook configurations are not copied into live. Live subscriptions must be configured and tested separately, and signature verification must use the live HMAC key rather than the different test key.

> [!warning] Disabling is not deletion
> Disabling a configuration queues events for that endpoint, and the captured page says queued events are delivered after reactivation. It also says configurations inactive for more than six months are automatically deleted. Plan maintenance and endpoint cutovers around both consequences rather than treating disablement as a durable pause.

quotes.text: Webhooks are HTTP callbacks sent to an endpoint on your server. Adyen requires you to use HTTPS endpoints with TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3.
quotes.location: ## 1. Expose an endpoint on your server, line 48

quotes.text: We require you to acknowledge every webhook event with a [successful HTTP response status code](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status#successful_responses), for example **200** or **202**. If we do not receive this response within 10 seconds for an reason, such as your server is down or your service is unavailable, all webhook events to your endpoint go to the [retry queue](/development-resources/webhooks/troubleshoot#retry-queue).

**Note:** Adyen does not provide a "copy" function for moving your webhook configurations from the test environment to the live environment. You need to configure all of your webhook subscriptions in the live environment.

If you are verifying HMAC signatures, make sure that you use the HMAC key from your [live Customer Area](https://ca-live.adyen.com/), which is different from the HMAC key from your [test Customer Area](https://ca-test.adyen.com/).

We will then queue all webhook events to this endpoint. You will receive the queued webhook events when you reactivate this endpoint configuration by selecting the **Active** checkbox.

Webhook configurations that have been inactive for more than six months are automatically deleted.
quotes.location: ## Disable and delete webhook configurations, lines 235-237
